summary: Intermittent SSO session owner_id shadowing prevents runbook impersonation and CLI elevation
description:
Issue summary: Multiple engineers report being unable to assume runbook/impersonation roles via the internal CLI and web runbook editor. Symptoms are intermittent and affect different users across org units.

Impact: Support engineers cannot escalate into customer runbooks or perform on-call emergency commands intermittently. Several paged incidents were delayed while the team worked around missing impersonation tokens.

Initial observation window: 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC - ongoing.

Observed behavior: After successful Okta SSO login, the internal session token occasionally contains an 'owner_id' claim that belongs to a different active session (shadowing). Authz checks then deny impersonation (403) or result in elevation requests that time out. Affected actions: runbook impersonation, temporary CLI elevation, and some console actions gated by just-in-time role grants.

Expected behavior: Each session should contain a single consistent identity/owner_id tied to the authenticated user and any requested delegated grants. Impersonation should succeed when the user has permission and the just-in-time approval is granted.

Environment details: Production auth-proxy fronting identity service (version v4.12.0). Okta as IdP, device-trust enabled for many users. Issue mostly reported in us-east region but one report from eu-west.

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1) Authenticate via SSO to console/CLI with device-trust flow.
2) Attempt to initiate runbook impersonation (web: Runbook -> Impersonate user X; CLI: redwood runbook impersonate --user X).
3) Observe 403 or 'impersonation failed: session mismatch' error.

Notes: The failure is not consistently reproducible in a single session — sometimes repeating the flow after 30-120s succeeds.
steps_to_reproduce: Login via Okta SSO with device-trust enabled
Issue runbook impersonation from web or CLI
Observe 403 or timeout; repeat to see intermittent success

comments: Ayesha Kapoor (Reporter) — 2026-03-10: Noticed spike in support pages around 21:00 UTC. Several engineers reported identical 403s when attempting to assume runbooks during an incident. Placing ticket to capture and track triage.

Diego Martinez (Assignee) — 2026-03-10: Triage started. Reproduced locally against staging by replaying auth-proxy cookies. Hypothesis: session cookie rotation + concurrent login can cause stale owner_id to be read from cookie cache. Collecting more traces.

Elena Park (SRE) — 2026-03-11: Added temporary logging on auth-proxy to dump session-token hashes (non-PII) and correlation id. Saw 4 traces where owner_id was swapped between two active sessions originating from same client IP but different devices.

Marco Chen (Identity eng) — 2026-03-12: Instrumented identity service to log token issuance events and nonce mapping. Found race in session-store snapshot write path when multiple SSO flows commit near-simultaneously for the same user via different devices. Working on a fix to make writes atomic.
Diego Martinez — 2026-03-13: Rolling out a hotfix to session-store which adds optimistic locking on session keys. Will monitor for 24 hours.
investigation_notes: Reproduction: Lowered concurrency window in staging and reproduced owner_id mismatch by firing two near-simultaneous device-trust SSO flows for same username.

Root cause hypothesis: session-store (redis snapshot + local in-memory cache) allowed a stale snapshot to be applied during concurrent session creation, causing the new session to inherit the owner_id from the other session's transient state.
Correlated alerts: Spike in runbook-service 403s at the same timestamps as session-store write contention metrics on redis-master-2 (see perf graph).
Temporary mitigations tested: added 100ms linear backoff on session-store write retry eliminated reproductions in staging under the test harness.
Edge case: cross-region redirected OIDC callbacks appear to exacerbate probability due to increased callback latency; eu-west report likely a compounded factor.
workaround: If impersonation fails, wait ~60-120s and retry. For urgent escalations, use alternate support account (with manual verification) or SSH into a bastion with SRE-approved out-of-band escalation. On-call runbook includes steps to use the temporary-bypass CLI token (audit-logged).
next_steps: Deploy optimistic-locking hotfix to session-store to prod us-east (Diego/Marco) — in progress
Monitor 403 rate for runbook-service and session-store write contention — SRE dashboard updated
Follow-up: review callback timeouts and add metrics for OIDC callback latency per region (Elena)
Postmortem and permanent fix: refactor session creation to single-source-of-truth commit path (identity eng roadmap)
